philosophy: Channel partners are owner-operators, often 20+ years in. They built the reputations of Polk, Definitive Tech, McIntosh, et al. Now they are treated like disposable assets because they do not hit spreadsheet numbers — but they cannot be fired either, because the bank *needs* a global distribution spine. AGF positions itself as the **future bank-roller, critically better than the devil they know**: lower price categories filled with curated third-party partner product, our line moving upward, the flagship landing just above Focal's consumer offering (~$5K USD).

partner_criteria.description: 20+ years in the segment; founder still actively involved.
Not currently captured by a PE roll-up or conglomerate parent.
Built the regional reputation of at least one premium brand (Polk, Definitive, McIntosh, etc.).
Custom install or appointment-based retail with technical staff.
Existing relationships with local venues, artists, or production communities.

revenue_model: **Curated third-party fills the price floor; AGF owns the price ceiling.** Lower categories backed by partner product (presented honestly, with brand-humility). AGF flagship lands just above Focal consumer (~$5K). The package — not the unit — is the negotiation. The Burmester €5,999 lesson applied across the whole channel.

territories.strategy: Stranded Polk/Definitive/McIntosh independents. Custom install + appointment-only retail.
Munich High-End channel relationships. UK boutique engineering brands as third-party fill.
Boutique audiophile retailers. Tone-meister culture alignment.
Selective premium retail; avoid PE-captured channels.
